comment: Mutation testing for the DOCUMENTATION PIPELINE. A SECOND config rather than entries in stryker-config.json because Stryker mutates one 'project' per run. This library exists as a non-test project precisely so it can be mutated: Stryker treats test projects as the test-projects, so a renderer living in DwarfMapper.Generator.Tests could never be a mutation target, and nothing would prove the doc tests catch a defect in the renderer itself. Run via scripts/housekeeping.ps1 -Mutation (needs: dotnet tool install -g dotnet-stryker --version 4.16.0). MEASURED 2026-08-19 on Stryker 4.16.0, against the WHOLE test suite (4,779 tests discovered), 12 logical cores, on an otherwise QUIET machine (~2 % CPU and no concurrent build at launch): score 83.10 % (236 detected of 284 scoreable — 233 killed + 3 timeout; 11 survived, 37 uncovered, 75 compile errors excluded), 5 min 57 s wall-clock. break is that score rounded DOWN to 83. THIS IS THE LEG'S FIRST COMPLETED RUN: the previous break of 70 was INHERITED AND HAD NEVER BEEN MEASURED — 'comment' sat INSIDE the 'stryker-config' object until 2026-08-16 (Stryker 4.16 rejects unknown keys there and refuses to run at all), and the 'mutate' globs were repo-root-relative until the same day, which matches nothing and produces a VACUOUS run that still exits 0. 83 is 13 points above the number it replaces, so the ratchet TIGHTENS. NOTE 1 — THERE IS DELIBERATELY NO 'additional-timeout' HERE, AND THAT IS A MEASURED DECISION, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. Its sibling stryker-config.json needed one because two of its timeouts were clock artifacts on mutants that cannot hang. All three timeouts in this leg GENUINELY HANG, so they are real detections and the default ceiling is correct: DocSnippetInjector.cs L39 deletes the 'i++' inside 'while (i < lines.Length)'; SnippetScanner.cs L138 and L139 delete the 'kept.RemoveAt(...)' inside 'while (kept.Count > 0 && string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(...))'. Each is an unconditional infinite loop. Their covering sets are 10, 1 and 1 tests — not the whole-suite geometry that manufactures a spurious timeout. Adding a 120 s cushion would only make three genuine hangs cost two extra minutes each. IF a Timeout ever appears here on a mutant that provably cannot hang (no loop, no unbounded recursion, no blocking call), raise 'additional-timeout' — never filter the test set. NOTE 2 — WHY THIS LEG IS FAST AND ITS SIBLING IS NOT: ZERO of its 284 scoreable mutants are 'static', so Stryker attributes per-test coverage to every one of them and the covering sets are tiny (1,603 test executions in total). The generator leg has 85 static mutants, each of which re-runs the entire suite, and it costs 21 minutes. The difference is coverage attribution, not test quality. NOTE 3 — RUNNING THIS LEG LOCALLY REWRITES TRACKED DOCUMENTATION, AND IT IS DESTRUCTIVE. The doc-generation tests WRITE into README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/diagnostics.md, docs/options.md and samples/DwarfMapper.Gallery/README.md, and the mutants under test are the code that writes them — so a mutant that truncates a document truncates the real file. The 2026-08-19 run left README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and docs/diagnostics.md EMPTIED (2,523 deleted lines across five files). It was reverted, not committed. After 'housekeeping.ps1 -Mutation', ALWAYS check 'git status' and 'git checkout --' the generated docs. In CI this is harmless (throwaway checkout, nothing committed); locally it is one 'git commit -a' away from deleting the documentation. This is a stronger form of the MutantControl pollution recorded in Issues/ledgers/E3-E1-report.md. NOTE 4 — the 'mutate' globs must be PROJECT-relative ('**/Name.cs'), never repo-root-relative: Stryker resolves them against src/DwarfMapper.DocTooling, so a repo-root path matches nothing, every mutant is dropped with 'Removed by mutate filter', and Stryker STILL EXITS 0. Assert-MutantsWereTested (scripts/housekeeping.ps1) exists for exactly that hazard; it counts scoreable statuses in the JSON report and returns 284 for this run. NOTE 5 — Stryker mutates and COMPILES the whole project regardless of these globs (568 mutants created; 183 dropped by the mutate filter; 75 rolled back as compile errors; 26 dropped by the block-already-covered filter; 247 tested plus 37 uncovered), and only then filters what is TESTED. The report therefore contains every file in the project; the five named here are the only ones carrying scoreable statuses, and that is the non-vacuity check to make. NOTE 6 — there is deliberately NO 'test-projects' key. It would be INERT: Stryker discovers the solution and enumerates EVERY test project in it, so such a list does not select the test set; see NOTE 3 in stryker-config.runtime.json for the measurement that established this. It was removed rather than corrected, so nothing here pretends to scope anything. NOTE 7 — the 11 survivors and 37 uncovered mutants are catalogued, with a real-hole-or-equivalent judgement for each, in Issues/ledgers/T3-mutation-survivors.md. Raise break only by killing survivors.
